Status code map
not-started - Not startedThe step's input record does not exist yet, or an earlier exit proof is not in the ledger.acts: The system starts the step when the ordering rule is met, and no agent or human does.
running - RunningThe step has a started row in the ledger and its time bound has not passed.acts: The step's own script and seats act, and the system watches the time bound.
blocked - BlockedThe step stopped after three retries or at a gate, and always carries a reason.acts: The system posts exactly one card to the owner with the reason, and the owner acts.
done - DoneEvery checklist box is ticked with its proof and the exit proof is in the ledger.acts: The system starts the next step, and no one else acts.
superseded - SupersededThe owner replaced the step, and the ledger row names what replaced it.acts: Only the owner sets this status.
Build mode rule

The factory's own governance never applies to the rebuild.

  • Old hooks, gates, guards, leases, watches and status rules are off for rebuild tickets.
  • Each new node ships dark and goes live by its own ticket with a named proof.
  • A rule that blocks a rebuild ticket is a defect in the rule, so the ticket proceeds and the rule gets a fix ticket.
  • The ledger records which rule bit.
Failure cases
stallNo progress is made past the step's time bound.detect: The system compares the last ledger row time and the output files with the time bound every minute. recover: The system ends the stalled work and starts a fresh seat or script run with the stall record attached. acts: The system acts and no agent or human does. retries: 3, then blocked
crashThe script, a seat, a pane or the session dies.detect: The system finds a started ledger row with no live worker and no exit proof. recover: The work resumes from the ledger, which is the only state, and reruns only what the exit proof lacks. acts: The system acts, and a cold session resumes by the recovery section if the system itself is down. retries: 3, then blocked
bad-outputThe exit proof fails its check.detect: The step's check runs on the exit proof and returns a failure. recover: A fresh seat retries with the failure attached, and never the seat that failed. acts: The system spawns the fresh seat and no agent or human does. retries: 3, then blocked
governance-interferenceAn old hook, gate, guard, lease, watch or status rule blocks a rebuild ticket.detect: The ticket's seat or the system reports a refusal that names the old rule. recover: The build-mode principle applies, so the ticket proceeds, the rule gets a fix ticket and the ledger row records which rule bit. acts: The system proceeds and cuts the fix ticket, and the owner is told only through the ledger. retries: 3, then blocked
Recovery

A cold session needs nothing but this XML, the ledger and main, and it reads them in the order below.

  • 1. rebuild/factory-rebuild-plan.xml - The plan on main, which names every step, proof and rule.
  • 2. rebuild/schema/factory-rebuild-plan.xsd - The contract the plan is validated against.
  • 3. ~/.local/state/coq/coq-jev-herdr-plugin/rebuild/2026/10/plan/ledger.tsv - The only record of what is started, done or blocked.
  • 4. ~/.local/state/coq/coq-jev-herdr-plugin/rebuild/2026/10/proofs/ - The exit proofs written so far.
  • 5. rebuild/README.md - Where every output lives and the cleanup command.

Run rebuild/bin/plan-validate.sh, then rebuild/bin/plan-to-rail.sh, then rebuild/rail.sh from a fresh worktree of main, and publish the built page to the URL in the latest checkpoint row.

  • Create a fresh worktree from origin/main and run the plan-validate.sh script, and stop if it fails.
  • Show the ledger with the ledger.sh --show option and find the first step with no complete row, which is the current step.
  • If the current step has a started row, check whether its exit proof paths exist and pass the step checklist.
  • If the proof exists and passes, append a complete row, otherwise start a fresh seat or script run with the failure attached.
  • If the last row for the step is blocked, read its ref and do nothing more, because the owner has one card waiting.
  • After every ledger row, rebuild the page with rail.sh and republish it to the same URL with the Artifact tool.
  • After the first publish, append a checkpoint row whose ref is the artifact URL, so a cold session republishes to the same URL.
